fields.name: friends
fields.description: The instance's IVenueFriends mixin. Left out of the schema where its module isn't installed.

fields.name: hidden
fields.description: Whether the venue is hidden.

fields.name: homeAudience
fields.description: The audience it comes from when that is another audience (linked here, or one to link); null for the audience's own venues and for a lone venue.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Its UUID.

fields.name: idCheckPolicy
fields.description: What its door must do with IDs where it is (doc/DOOR_ID_CHECKS.md). Null unless the viewer can work its door.

fields.name: idChecks
fields.description: Its door's ID check log: every check still kept, newest first. Null unless the viewer can work its door.

fields.name: karaoke
fields.description: The instance's IVenueKaraoke mixin, when available. Null unless it has the karaoke facet (its facets).

fields.name: linked
fields.description: Whether it is another audience's venue, its home (doc/LINKED_VENUES.md): listed here by a link, this audience curates its listing (locale, hidden, order, showsEvents) and its home audience runs everything else.

fields.name: listed
fields.description: False for a community space (its Community space tag), like a pride center that hosts events: listed after the venues to go out to and left out of nearby (doc/ORGANIZERS.md).

fields.name: listing
fields.description: This audience's link to it, when linked: null for its own venues.

fields.name: liveActivity
fields.description: What its screens show as their live activity now, as the lineup on now has set it (bingo, trivia, sing-along, prompts); null while nothing on now sets one.

fields.name: localRules
fields.description: Its own rules (age policy, licence, last call), as approved; null when none were.

fields.name: locale
fields.description: The city or area containing this venue.

fields.name: location
fields.description: Its geographic location.

fields.name: marqueeHiddenSlogans
fields.description: The Hot Mess slogan slides (by id, as in hotmess.social/marquee/slogans.json) the venue turned off on its TV marquee; every other one shows. New lines show until the venue turns them off.

fields.name: marqueePosters
fields.description: The standard posters its TV may rotate in (slogan slides): its audience's own and AudienceKit's, the adult ones only where it's flagged. Includes the ones it turned off (marqueeHiddenSlogans), for its picker.

fields.name: marqueeSlogans
fields.description: Whether its TV marquee (Velvet, the web sign at hotmess.social/venues/<id>/display) shows Hot Mess slogan slides between the lineup: on unless the venue turns them off.

fields.name: music
fields.description: The instance's IVenueMusic mixin. Left out of the schema where its module isn't installed.

fields.name: musicLicensing
fields.description: Its music licensing: the public performance licenses it holds, its linked music services (Soundtrack, Rockbot, Mood Media, TouchTunes) and what needs attention. Its managers only; null for everyone else.

fields.name: musicNowPlaying
fields.description: What its licensed business music services play right now, each zone of its linked Soundtrack account or its Rockbot zone with the queue, read with the API key it linked (linkVenueMusicService) and cached for 15 seconds. Empty without one. Its managers and Velvet devices only; null for everyone else.

fields.name: musixmatch
fields.description: Its own Musixmatch key, which its sing-along screens use before its audience's and AudienceKit's (setVenueMusixmatchKey); null without one, and for everyone but its managers.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The venue's name, or its Facebook page's.

fields.name: order
fields.description: Its display order.

fields.name: ordering
fields.description: The instance's IVenueOrdering mixin, when available. Null unless it has the ordering facet (its facets).

fields.name: pairUp
fields.description: The instance's IVenuePairUp mixin, when available. Null unless it has the pair_up facet (its facets).

fields.name: pairUpEnabled
fields.description: Whether Quickie is on there (Venue.pairUp): on unless the venue opted out.

fields.name: people
fields.description: The instance's IVenuePeople mixin. Left out of the schema where its module isn't installed.

fields.name: photoUrl
fields.description: The photo's CDN URL, if there is one.

fields.name: photography
fields.description: The instance's IEventPhotos mixin, when available.

fields.name: ping
fields.description: The instance's IPingFeed mixin, when available.

fields.name: point
fields.description: Where it is, as WKT: its location's point.

fields.name: posterArt
fields.description: Its generated backgrounds and commissioned posters, newest first. Whoever may change it sees them all; everyone else, the READY ones, which are made to be shared (Backstage).

fields.name: posts
fields.description: The instance's IPosts mixin. Left out of the schema where its module isn't installed.

fields.name: profile
fields.description: The instance's IListingProfile mixin. Left out of the schema where its module isn't installed.

fields.name: promoPlacements
fields.description: Promoted cards booked for the venue or its events, newest first, each with its one metric: different people who saw it a week.

fields.name: promoTier
fields.description: Its rate card tier (small, mid, large), which its own promoted cards are priced at; the cheapest until the audience sets one.

fields.name: reportedClosed
fields.description: Whether it was reported closed and that isn't decided yet: left out of tonight's views, its page kept.

fields.name: requests
fields.description: The instance's IVenueRequests mixin. Left out of the schema where its module isn't installed.

fields.name: rollUp
fields.description: Items linked to it or to anything under it (a venue's events and series, a locale's venues), one row per item, newest first. Only linked items, unless an admin asks for suggested or rejected ones too.

args.name: itemKinds
args.description: Only these kinds of items.

args.name: limit
args.description: At most this many (up to 200).

args.name: statuses
args.description: Links in these states; anything but LINKED needs an admin.

fields.name: rooms
fields.description: The instance's IRooms mixin, when available to the viewer.

fields.name: safetyAlerts
fields.description: Safety alerts guests sent here, newest first: the ones still open or picked up, and the ones closed in the last 12 hours. Its managers, Velvet devices with moderation and the audience's admins.

fields.name: safetyPoster
fields.description: Its live safety poster code, or null before anyone made one (issueSafetyPoster). Its managers and every Velvet device of the venue read it.

fields.name: safetyShift
fields.description: Whether the caller's device hears this venue's safety alerts (setSafetyShift).

fields.name: safetyStaffOnShift
fields.description: Whether anyone on shift here hears safety alerts right now; the app offers other ways to get help when not.

fields.name: screenBackdrops
fields.description: The pictures Velvet's screens may show behind the board, in the order to show them: banners without text, Google photos without text, then ones that are mostly text.

fields.name: slideshows
fields.description: Its slideshows for its screens, the default poster list first. Its managers and devices only.

fields.name: spotify
fields.description: Its own connected Spotify account, which reads the playlists it owns for its nights before the audience's (connectVenueSpotify). Its managers only; null for everyone else.

fields.name: tagLayers
fields.description: Its tags in layers: its own, its regular nights and its upcoming events’ one-off tags (doc/design-system/TribesAndTags.md). For a venue screen, not lists.

args.name: includeHidden
args.description: Add the regular nights its staff hid. Only for its managers and admins; ignored for anyone else.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Its audience tags, including tags connected to module facets, by name.

fields.name: taskTemplates
fields.description: Its lineup task templates, in order. Empty for anyone but whoever keeps them (its managers; an event's hosts too).

fields.name: tickets
fields.description: The instance's IVenueTickets mixin. Left out of the schema where its module isn't installed.

fields.name: trivia
fields.description: The instance's IVenueTrivia mixin. Left out of the schema where its module isn't installed.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the record was last updated.

fields.name: velvetSubscription
fields.description: Its Velvet subscription: whether it pays for Velvet itself and whether its tools are open. Its owner, managers and staff only.

fields.name: viewerRole
fields.description: What you are to it: its owner, a manager, staff or an admin; null when none of these.

fields.name: visibility
fields.description: Whether full listing details are public on the web.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description: A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a __DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a mutation operation.

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a subscription operation.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment definition.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_SPREAD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment spread.

enumValues.name: INLINE_FRAGMENT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: VARIABLE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a variable definition.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an argument definition.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an interface definition.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a union definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM_VALUE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum value definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object type definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object field definition.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description: Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name and description, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields` and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

directives.description: App Clips call this field (HOT_MESS, VELVET, BACKSTAGE), so their small clients (doc/APP_CLIP_API.md) depend on it. Keep it working for clips people already have: add a replacement and deprecate rather than change it. It is a marking, not security: @requires is enforced as on any other field.

directives.name: deprecated

directives.name: endpoint

Without it a field is on every endpoint where its type is reachable. It is visibility, not security: @requires is enforced on every endpoint.

args.name: in

args.name: if
args.description: Included when true.

directives.name: mixin
directives.description: Declares a module-owned interface available as an edge on eligible object types.

args.name: extensionKey
args.description: The module that owns this contract.

args.name: field
args.description: The generated edge name.

args.name: null
args.description: False when the edge is never null where its module is installed; where it is not, the edge is left out of the schema.

args.name: on
args.description: Eligible GraphQL object type names.

args.name: tag
args.description: Makes it a facet: the key of the tag (Tag.facet) a record carries for the edge to resolve on it. Null on records without it; they list it in their facets when they have it.

directives.name: oneOf
directives.description: Requires that exactly one field must be supplied and that field must not be `null`.

directives.name: requires
directives.description: The permissions that let a caller use this field, any one of them: each `namespace:action:scope`, where namespace is the owning module (or a core area), action is read, write, moderate or admin, and scope is * (anything in the audience), mine (what the caller manages), my_troupes (troupes they act for), venue (a venue device's venue), self (their own records) or door (venues whose door they work). Without it a field is public.

args.name: permissions
args.description: Any one of these permits the field.

directives.name: skip
directives.description: Directs the executor to skip this field or fragment when the `if` argument is true.

args.name: if
args.description: Skipped when true.

directives.name: specifiedBy
directives.description: Exposes a URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.

args.name: url
args.description: The URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.
